The corporate deal team was led by Orange County/Bay Area partner Nima Movahedi and Bay Area partner Tad Freese, with associates Christopher Siino and Chloe Wallace.

Advice on intellectual property matters was provided by associate Andrew Abokhair. The articles do not give further statements from the companies or their representatives. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the announced fundraise and its stated purposes. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Anthropic AI finds 29,000 open source bugs, 516 patched
stories.Summary:
Anthropic's new OSS Scanner, part of its Cyber Mission, identified more than 29,000 potential vulnerabilities in widely used open source projects over six months, the company said. The tool was launched last week. Claude models are finding possible bugs faster than human researchers can verify them, according to Anthropic. A human review pipeline using six external security research firms has processed only about 6,000 findings.

A disclosure dashboard showed that 5,674 of 6,123 reviewed findings were confirmed valid by October 2, but only 516 vulnerabilities had been patched upstream by that date. Anthropic sent 6,157 findings to maintainers, resulting in 584 CVE and GitHub Security Advisory identifiers. About 23,000 candidate vulnerabilities remain unreviewed by human teams. Anthropic offers an optional fast-track that sends unvalidated reports directly to maintainers, and nearly 5,000 such reports have gone to maintainers who requested them. Expert penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings from an early scanner version across 48 projects, and 85 cleared the bar for disclosure, with 11 of the remaining 12 being real bugs that duplicated known issues and only one a false positive.

Anton Arapov, director of OpenSSL Corporation, said the reports matched and sometimes beat human researchers, and that a report with a working exploit means the job is basically done for an engineer. Todd Ouska, founder of wolfSSL, said 72 of 74 reports his team received were valid, and five became CVEs. PostgreSQL committer Noah Misch said several reports arrived with fixes the project could use nearly as-is, and credited fast-track access with addressing new issues before a general availability release. Daniel Stenberg, founder of The cURL Project, said the scanner found multiple issues in curl, including one of the worst vulnerabilities the project has seen in recent years.

Anthropic restricts access to established open source projects that meet OSS-Fuzz-style eligibility criteria, verifies that applicants are core maintainers, and expects participating projects to be keeping up with high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities already reported to them. Eligible maintainers can receive free Claude Max 20x subscriptions. Under the disclosure terms, maintainers can work at their own pace on unvalidated scanner findings, but a report later validated by Anthropic's standard program can be disclosed 90 days after human confirmation. Anthropic acknowledged that maintainers reported inflated severity ratings and cases where the scanner misunderstood a project's threat model.

Articles.Title: anthropic ai finds 29000 open source bugs 516 patched

stories.Headline: Meesho uses AI for 75 per cent orders, 62 per cent customer queries
stories.Summary:
Meesho now uses artificial intelligence across much of its business, according to Pratik Kumar, the company's head of engineering. Its Prism system drives nearly 75 per cent of orders through personalised ranking. Its AI customer support agent, Chorus, handles 62 per cent of user queries. Kumar oversees technology and AI-related initiatives at the company. Prism recommends products using signals such as demographics, geography, device usage, browsing behaviour, product clicks and ignored listings.

The system is built to work out what shoppers want even when they arrive without a clear plan to buy. Meesho also uses an AI system called TrendPulse to anticipate demand and help sellers prepare inventory ahead of emerging trends. Kumar gave Navratri as an example, noting that shoppers look for particular colours of clothing depending on local customs. Kumar said AI is used across product discovery, demand forecasting, customer support, voice-led shopping, fraud prevention, address prediction, logistics and seller enablement. Its Vaani agent lets users find products, understand information, add items to carts and complete transactions by voice.

On the seller side, AI agents handle queries about financial journeys, payouts, monetisation and campaign creation, which cuts dependence on human intervention. Meesho's in-house Bharat-MLStack has reduced AI inference and model-related costs by around 60-70 per cent compared with external providers, he said. Meesho currently has approximately 960,000 transacting sellers on its platform. AI is being used to simplify seller onboarding, particularly for sellers in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: meesho uses ai for 75 per cent orders 62 per cent customer queries

stories.Headline: Indonesia Promotes Child Protection from AI Risks in UNESCO Meeting
stories.Summary:
Indonesia pushed for global rules to protect children from digital technology and artificial intelligence risks at a UNESCO meeting in Paris. IGAK Satrya Wibawa, Indonesia's deputy permanent representative to UNESCO, spoke on the fifth day of the 225th Session of the UNESCO Executive Board on Friday, October 16, 2026. Indonesia supports building a safe, healthy, inclusive digital ecosystem that puts children first. Satrya said the question is not just whether children can use digital devices, but when, for what purpose, and at what stage of development technology best helps learning.

The session discussed two main initiatives. The first is a Pakistan proposal called UNESCO Guidelines on the Use of Digital Devices by Children and Young Adults and Its Impact on Foundational Learning and Cognitive Abilities, which Indonesia supports along with other UNESCO members. It calls for international studies on how smartphones, tablets, and other devices affect literacy, numeracy, attention span, critical thinking, and cognitive development. The second initiative is a plan for an international instrument to protect and empower young people in the AI era, covering social media, algorithms, digital games, virtual worlds, chatbots, and AI companions. The proposed instrument is a recommendation scheduled for consideration at the UNESCO General Conference in November 2027 through an expedited procedure.

Satrya said policies on children's use of technology must be based on scientific evidence, not just concern about new technology. He said no single policy is automatically right for all countries, since excessive device use can interfere with learning in some places while technology is the main bridge to education in others. He called for involving schools, families, civil society, researchers, and technology companies, so protection goes beyond limiting use and also builds children's ability to use technology responsibly. He said protection and empowerment must go hand in hand, and that the goal is not to keep children away from technology but to ensure they use it safely, critically, creatively, and responsibly.

At the national level, Indonesia has a digital governance framework to protect children through Government Regulation Number 17 of 2025 on the Governance of the Implementation of Electronic Systems in the Protection of Children, known as PP TUNAS. UNESCO also proposed an international study with a network of global university researchers, including UNESCO Chairs and the UNITWIN network. The results are planned as the basis for a report and draft guidelines to be discussed at the 226th Session of the UNESCO Executive Board. Indonesia hopes the two initiatives will produce global guidelines that respect human rights, reduce the digital divide, and open opportunities for young people to take part wisely in digital transformation.

Articles.Title: Indonesia Promotes Child Protection from AI Risks in UNESCO Meeting - VOI.ID

stories.Headline: Initiative by IMDA, AI Verify Foundation tests AI accuracy, trustworthiness in real-world scenarios - Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB)
stories.Summary:
Doctors at Changi General Hospital are testing generative artificial intelligence to summarise medical reports and give recommendations on clinical surveillance. Regulatory technology firm Tookitaki uses the technology to investigate possible money laundering and fraud cases. Earlier in 2025, the Infocomm Media Development Authority and the AI Verify Foundation rolled out an initiative on real-world uses of generative AI. The AI Verify Foundation is a not-for-profit subsidiary of IMDA that tackles pressing issues arising from AI.

Between March and May, 17 organisations across 10 sectors, including human resources, healthcare and finance, had their generative AI applications assessed by specialist testing firms. The findings were published on 29 May. The initiative is called the Global AI Assurance Pilot. Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information Tan Kiat How spoke on 29 May, the last day of the Asia Tech x Singapore conference at Capella Singapore.

Clinical Associate Professor Chow Weien, chief data and digital officer at Changi General Hospital, told The Straits Times the initiative helped the hospital design a more robust and reliable way of testing its AI models. Tookitaki founder and chief executive Abhishek Chatterjee told the paper the experience made the firm's AI model more auditable and let it add guardrails against AI hallucinations. AI Verify Foundation executive director Shameek Kundu said earlier initiatives focused on testing AI models, while this pilot aimed to test reliability in real-world scenarios. He said the aim is to make generative AI use boring and predictable.

IMDA and the AI Verify Foundation said in a statement that human experts were essential at every stage of testing, from designing tests to interpreting results. A testing starter kit for generative AI applications has also been developed as voluntary guidelines for businesses. IMDA is holding a four-week public consultation on the starter kit, which ends on 25 June, and feedback can be emailed to aigov@imda.gov.sg. Tan also announced that AI Singapore will sign a memorandum of understanding with the United Nations Development Programme to advance AI literacy in developing countries.

Articles.Title: Initiative by IMDA, AI Verify Foundation tests AI accuracy, trustworthiness in real-world scenarios - Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB)

stories.Headline: Philippine AI hub raises concerns over transparency, community displacement - CNA
stories.Summary:
The Philippines plans to build a large artificial intelligence industrial hub as part of its commitment to the US-led Pax Silica initiative. In April, the country signed a non-binding declaration aimed at countering the world's reliance on China for advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure. The project is planned for Capas, Tarlac, according to CNA's report from the area. Locals worry about the lack of consultations and transparency around the project.

The declaration the Philippines signed in April is non-binding and seeks to reduce dependence on China for advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure. The planned hub is described as sprawling and is tied to the Pax Silica initiative led by the United States. The report did not give the project's cost, size or construction timeline. It also did not say how many people could be displaced or when work might begin.

Responsibility for the project rests with the Philippine government, which signed the April declaration and is pursuing the hub. The articles do not name any official who commented on the project. They also do not include statements from government representatives or from the companies involved. Residents in Capas, Tarlac, are the ones raising concerns about consultation and transparency.

The context is the wider Pax Silica effort to shift advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure away from China. The report was the last in a two-part series by correspondent Jhesset Enano. It did not say what happens next, such as whether consultations will be held or when construction could start. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Philippine AI hub raises concerns over transparency, community displacement - CNA

stories.Headline: PM Wong calls for an independent global body to oversee AI policies - CNA
stories.Summary:
Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong called for an independent, global watchdog to govern artificial intelligence, speaking at an event organised by local bank DBS. He said the body could audit AI systems and progressively tighten requirements. He said this would keep frontier AI development safe without stifling innovation. The report was published on 12 October 2026.

The proposal is for an independent body that would oversee AI policies worldwide. Under the plan, the watchdog could audit AI systems, and its requirements could be tightened over time. The aim given was to keep frontier AI development safe while not stifling innovation. The articles give no further numbers, dates or names for the plan.

Wong is the person behind the call, and he set out the idea in his remarks at the DBS event. He said the body should be independent and global. He said it could audit AI systems and tighten requirements progressively. He said frontier AI development should stay safe without innovation being stifled.

The articles give little context beyond the speech and do not say what happens next. They do not say who would set up the body or when it might begin work. They do not say whether any government or organisation has responded to the call. More to follow.

Articles.Title: PM Wong calls for an independent global body to oversee AI policies - CNA

stories.Headline: IMF says AI investment keeps global growth around 3%, with major Asia benefits - CNA
stories.Summary:
International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday, October 12, 2026, that strong investment in AI infrastructure is keeping global growth at around 3 per cent. She spoke in Bangkok on the first day of a weeklong set of meetings of the IMF and World Bank. The artificial intelligence investment boom was already delivering a demand shock and an investment shock, she said. Georgieva said AI is already here, whether people love it or hate it.

The IMF forecast global growth at 3 per cent in 2026 in July, and it will release an updated outlook on Tuesday. Georgieva said the AI boom could boost growth in advanced Asian economies by a half to one full percentage point, and in emerging Asian economies by 0.2 to 0.8 percentage point. The IMF estimates that AI could lead to 40 per cent of jobs being augmented, downgraded or eliminated over time. An initial study showed that 10 per cent of jobs in the US already required AI skills.

Georgieva said AI amounts to a slow-moving tsunami with profound consequences for jobs, growth, education and how governments raise revenue through taxation. She said the shift from labour to capital is behind that concern. The US, China and India are the most important producers in the AI supply chain, she said, but many firms building the needed infrastructure are in Asia, including Thailand, the host of this year's meetings. Some 18,000 people are expected to attend the meetings this week, including finance officials from the IMF's 191 members.

World Bank President Ajay Banga said the development bank was focused on leveraging small AI, which is not dependent on large language models, to generate productivity gains for farmers, healthcare systems, educators and others in emerging markets. Singapore's President Tharman Shanmugaratnam said governments should address how AI was reducing job opportunities for graduates. He said the first rung in employment, the first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand. He also warned that AI is going to widen divergence between developing and advanced economies if the world is too passive about it.

Articles.Title: IMF says AI investment keeps global growth around 3%, with major Asia benefits - CNA

stories.Headline: ‘Diverging’ trajectories: Taiwan dethrones South Korea atop global markets as AI trade widens
stories.Summary:
Taiwan’s Taiex Index has overtaken South Korea’s Kospi as the top performer among more than 90 equity indices tracked by Bloomberg in 2026. The Taiex is up 72 per cent this year, while the Kospi ranks second with gains of about 65 per cent. The Taiex beat the Kospi by about 23 percentage points last quarter, the widest margin since the turn of the century. Earnings upgrades for Taiwan also outpaced those for South Korea for the first time since March 2025.

About 40 per cent of fund managers surveyed by Bank of America in September said they were overweight on Taiwan, versus 25 per cent for South Korea. When asked which market would benefit most from the next phase of the AI cycle, 35 per cent chose Taiwan and just 5 per cent picked South Korea. The Taiex trades at about 18 times its one-year forward estimated earnings, while the Kospi trades at around 5.5 times. About 10 per cent of the Taiex’s stocks have at least doubled in 2026, compared with 4.1 per cent for the Kospi and 5.7 per cent for Japan’s Nikkei 225.

Vikas Pershad, a portfolio manager at M&G Investments in Singapore, said the difference is not simply the amount of AI exposure but the nature of the earnings behind it. He said Taiwan offers a broader and deeper opportunity set, with earnings coming from volume, making upgrades broader and stickier, while South Korea’s near-term earnings come from price. Societe Generale strategists including Rajat Agarwal wrote that they keep a preference for Taiwan over Korean equities given the diverging earnings growth trajectories. They said memory price appreciation is expected to slow over coming quarters before normalisation in 2028 as Chinese competition rises.

Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunged between 19 per cent and 33 per cent in the three months ended September, after a six-quarter winning streak driven by surging memory chip prices. South Korea’s market leadership remains heavily concentrated in those two chipmakers, leaving it more vulnerable as doubts emerge over how much longer the memory upcycle can run. The counter view is that AI-related demand will worsen the semiconductor supply shortage and keep prices for high-bandwidth memory chips supported. Peter Lee, a managing director at Citigroup, said last week that investors should start buying shares of firms like Samsung and SK Hynix because the market is underestimating how much high-bandwidth memory will be needed in 2027.

Articles.Title: ‘Diverging’ trajectories: Taiwan dethrones South Korea atop global markets as AI trade widens - The Business Times

stories.Headline: Researchers in Australia develop AI tool to assess stroke risk - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Researchers in Australia have developed an artificial intelligence model that analyzes DNA to identify genetic risk factors for stroke. The study identified 18 genetic variants linked to ischemic stroke, the most common type of stroke. People in the highest genetic risk group had a 22 percent higher chance of stroke than those in the lower-risk group, according to a statement from the University of Technology Sydney. The team used a type of AI known as a transformer to train the model on thousands of genetic variations.

Researchers tested the AI model using genetic and health data from the UK Biobank and a large U.S. database. The model was more accurate than previous genetic risk tools at distinguishing people who had suffered a stroke from those who had not. The study also identified the gene EDEM2 in brain cortex tissue as a key contributor to stroke susceptibility, providing a target for further research. The work was released in a statement from the University of Technology Sydney.

Researchers are now developing a multimodal AI tool that combines genetic assessments with other modes of data. These include health and lifestyle surveys, scans and imaging, to improve risk assessment for stroke and other diseases. The statement said the model paves the way for more personalized risk assessments and prevention. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Researchers in Australia develop AI tool to assess stroke risk - Xinhua

stories.Headline: China Focus: From smart sensors to AI robots, technology transforming China's elderly care - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Smart devices in the homes of more than 600 elderly people living alone in Luyang District of Hefei, the capital of Anhui Province, send alerts to community workers. The devices include door sensors and smoke detectors, and they warn workers when no door activity has been detected for more than 24 hours or when a smoke detector is triggered. Most of the residents are aged 80 or above. The system is part of a government-funded elderly care program launched in 2025, according to Zhao Fei, director of the Luyang district office of the committee on aging. Around a dozen alerts are generated and handled each day.

When an alert is triggered, a three-tier response mechanism involving family members, community workers and community officials is activated so each warning gets appropriate follow-up, Zhao said. He said the mix of smart warnings and human intervention builds a safety net for elderly people living alone at home, and that finding such risks through human inspections alone would be nearly impossible. In the Shulu Community Service Center in Hefei high-tech zone, a robot equipped with cameras and powered by large AI models screens the mental health of elderly people, said Liu Li, head of the center's social affairs department. It analyzes facial expressions, eye features and subtle body movements and combines these with physiological signals to produce a report on a person's mental state.

Anhui Sanlian Robot Technology Co., Ltd. has introduced its fourth-generation lower-limb exoskeleton, which uses AI to adapt assistance to users' movements. Marketing director Wu Xianchun said the device detects when users need extra support as they lift their legs and reduces assistance when they stop, allowing people with walking difficulties to move more naturally. The exoskeletons were first developed mainly for postoperative leg rehabilitation and activities such as mountain climbing, and are now used mainly in elderly care facilities, with demand shifting toward helping older people exercise their legs and improve everyday mobility. Wu said better algorithms make devices smarter, while improved manufacturing and mass production help enhance quality and cut the cost of parts such as batteries and motors.

Official data shows China's population aged 60 and above exceeded 323 million by the end of 2025, about 23 percent of the national total. Intelligent massage and companion robots are being used in Beijing for physical therapy and companionship, some nursing homes in Shanghai have adopted smart mattresses to monitor residents' health, and virtual reality devices are used for rehabilitation training among older people in Shenzhen. China's market for elderly care service robots is expected to exceed 10 billion yuan, about 1.5 billion U.S. dollars, in 2026, according to a research report released by the China Software Testing Center this year. Liu Sizhe, an 18-year-old student at the University of Science and Technology of China, launched a startup this year and led a team in developing an AI-based system for preliminary screening for Alzheimer's disease, which analyzes speech rate and responses during casual conversations on a mobile phone or tablet. Liu said his grandparents inspired the project and that he does not want the elderly to be left behind by technological advances.

Articles.Title: China Focus: From smart sensors to AI robots, technology transforming China's elderly care - Xinhua

stories.Headline: DeepSeek unveils faster, cheaper AI model, with improved performance
stories.Summary:
DeepSeek released an updated AI model called DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on Saturday, according to the Global Times. The Chinese start-up said the new model is an upgraded version of V4.1-Flash, which came out last month. DeepSeek said the update brings stronger benchmark results, faster task completion and shorter outputs than the earlier version. The company also said the model is designed to improve reasoning, coding and AI agent capabilities.

DeepSeek said V4.1-Flash-1017 scored 77.0 on the software development benchmark DeepSWE v1.1, compared with 74.0 for Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and 73.0 for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. In the AutomationBench workflow automation test, it scored 60.5, ahead of Opus 5's 50.3. The company said the model's API now supports new Search and Fetch interfaces, priced at 5 yuan, or $0.75, per 1,000 requests. DeepSeek said the expense per coding task is about $0.20, far less than one-tenth that of comparable US models, and the fee per 1 million API output tokens is $0.59 off-peak and $1.19 at peak, against $20 for GPT-5.6 Sol and $25 for Claude Opus 5.

DeepSeek said the model's gains come from reinforcement learning training based on self-feedback, which it said helps with building complete projects from scratch, including game development and 3D modeling. Liu Gang, chief economist at the Chinese Institute of New Generation AI Development Strategies, told the Global Times that stronger coding and reasoning, faster tasks and lower output costs matter because they target productivity, affordability and reliability. He said Chinese AI companies have shown they can keep iterating and optimizing models and drive industry innovation. The report also said Shanghai-based StartLux took the top spot on Hugging Face's Decision Index 0.3.2 leaderboard, with its StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B Instant model scoring 69.1 among 173 publicly reproducible models.

Articles.Title: DeepSeek unveils faster, cheaper AI model, with improved performance - Global Times

stories.Headline: Why are Chinese tokens gaining popularity overseas in the AI era?
stories.Summary:
Xiamen in East China's Fujian Province completed its first export of token-based AI services to Ethiopia, the Xiamen Municipal Bureau of Commerce said on September 3. The first deal involved 2.7 billion tokens, and transaction volume passed 10 billion tokens within a week of the service's launch. The service is powered by a homegrown large language model from Xiamen-based Unisound. An Ethiopian e-commerce company sends requests to the model in Xiamen, pays for the tokens it uses, and gets back things like multilingual subtitles and dubbed audio.

In Shantou, in Guangdong Province, a pilot zone validated the full commercial process for token exports in late April. Average daily token use there rose from 100 million to 100 billion in less than five months, a 1,000-fold increase. Shantou Kedom iLink Technology was set up in the zone in May, and its general manager, Li Wenyi, said daily token use passed 1 billion in just over four months, growing about 15 to 20 percent month on month. In Nanning, in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, the Wuxiang Cloud Valley token factory can produce up to 200 billion tokens an hour.

Lu Yang, general manager of Unisound, said Ethiopian clients chose Chinese token services for a very practical reason: price. They had tried US models such as GPT, but the cost was too high, while Chinese services are far more cost-effective. Li said that for the same computing traffic and performance, his company's price can be one-third of Western models like GPT. Zhang Xianghong, a professor at Beijing Jiaotong University, said tokens are a standardized intelligent service built from data, models and computing power. Wang Jiye, former deputy chief information officer of State Grid Corporation of China, said token processing uses vast amounts of electricity, and China's power industry has advantages in output, stability and equipment supply.

Industry figures said China's lower electricity prices help make its computing services cheaper. Yang Yang, general manager of the token business at ChinaDataPay.com, said Chinese token supply is a rigid demand for content creators in Southeast Asia. Wu Yongzhan, deputy general manager of the token business at Runjian, said the aim is computing power on demand, billed by usage like water and electricity, which lowers the threshold for smaller developers in developing countries. Zhang said the token industry is still at a very early, exploratory stage, but he believes tokens may one day become an important strategic resource, and that China is bound to become a major global hub for token production and consumption.

Articles.Title: Why are Chinese tokens gaining popularity overseas in the AI era? - Global Times

stories.Headline: Exclusive: NVIDIA’s Vera Team Says Chiplet Designs Sacrificed Single-Threaded Performance For Core Counts, And Agentic AI Is Now Forcing A Reversal
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA's Vera team spoke with Wccftech in an interview published on October 18, 2026, about the company's new Vera CPU. The team said data center chips moved toward many cores and away from per-core speed as cloud providers grew. That shift came at the cost of single-threaded performance and instructions per cycle, the team said. Agentic AI is now forcing a reversal, and Vera is the result.

Vera is NVIDIA's first CPU built for agentic AI, the team said. It is 1.5 times faster than Grace and 2 times faster than the leading x86 part on agentic workloads, with a 1.6 times advantage on a geometric mean basis. The chip uses a single monolithic compute die, a custom LPDDR5X memory subsystem and the second-generation NVIDIA Scalable Coherent Fabric. It also uses spatial multithreading, which sets aside one worker thread and one I/O thread per core, and Phoronix found about a 20 percent performance uplift from it.

The team said NVIDIA first designed Grace as a host node to feed GPUs in a rack. It later saw a need for pure racks of standalone CPUs to handle agent tool calls and reinforcement learning, and Vera is now sold as a standalone CPU as well as part of the Vera-Rubin stack. On disaggregation, the team said AI infrastructure is splitting into specialized setups, such as separate clusters for pre-fill and decode in inference. It could not say whether NVIDIA plans something like SK Hynix's HTPU, which puts about 100 tiny processors inside an SSD.

The team said GPUs remain among the most valuable assets in an AI factory, so the CPU must finish its sequential work quickly to keep them busy. Vera is meant to sit in what the team called the top-right quadrant, with both high single-threaded performance and high throughput. The articles do not say when Vera ships or how it is priced. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Exclusive: NVIDIA’s Vera Team Says Chiplet Designs Sacrificed Single-Threaded Performance For Core Counts, And Agentic AI Is Now Forcing A Reversal - Wccftech

stories.Headline: Why Personal AI Skills Fail Inside Organizations - Seoul Economic Daily
stories.Summary:
Leaders who use generative AI fluently often assume that spreading it across an organization will be just as easy, and the article calls that a dangerous illusion. The piece, published by Seoul Economic Daily on October 19, 2026, says the AI one person experiences and the AI an organization must carry are problems on different levels. For an individual, handing a report to a chatbot is a reversible experiment where the cost of failure is close to zero. Inside a company, AI becomes the basis for judgments shared by many people, so a single error ripples widely and the organization must answer for accountability. The article says individual use of AI needs no governance, while organizational use makes governance everything.

It draws a line between digital transformation, which is deterministic and must always produce the same result from the same input, and AI transformation, which is probabilistic and recommends the most plausible option rather than the correct answer. It says bringing imperfect AI, with problems such as hallucination, into core operational areas without a safety net is reckless. Enterprise resource planning is described as the safety net, a policy engine that checks budget status, compliance and the approver's signing authority before a purchase goes through. The article gives the example of AI recommending an advance order for 500 tons from supplier B with 85% probability, which must not trigger the order on its own. The article places responsibility on leaders, saying their questions must change.

Pulling up current sales figures is something a staff member can do, but executives should be asking why figures fell and what must be fixed. It says answering that requires the organization's data to be recorded without error and AI to find hidden links on top of it. It also says that as AI evolves into agents that draw up their own plans and move across multiple systems, people must verify and approve the plan itself in advance. The article says future competitiveness will be decided not by superficial skill in handling AI but by how precisely and rigorously the real world has been structured so that AI can perform. It says this shift, which lets leaders ask why and what must be fixed, will guide an organization toward genuinely sustainable innovation.

Articles.Title: Why Personal AI Skills Fail Inside Organizations - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Pohang Steel Complex Launches AI Project With 15 Partners - Seoul Economic Daily
stories.Summary:
The Research Institute of Industrial Science and Technology said on the 18th that work has begun on a project to apply artificial intelligence across the Pohang Steel Industrial Complex in North Gyeongsang Province. The institute held a kickoff meeting for the Pohang Smart Green AI Transformation Pilot Industrial Complex Project on Oct. 15 and 16 at Lahan Select in Gyeongju. The Pohang complex was selected in a competition run by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for AX pilot industrial complexes. A total of 23.5 billion won in central and local government funding will be invested over four years, from this year through 2029.

The project will support AI adoption at individual companies and build a foundation for manufacturing innovation across the whole complex. It will set up a joint support system so that small and mid-sized companies without in-house development capacity or investment capability can also use AI technology. During the project period, the complex will host an AX comprehensive support center and a convergence test bed linking virtual environments with actual production sites. Companies will be able to verify whether AI technology can be applied on the shop floor and move ahead with adoption. Dongkuk Steel and Jeil Technos will lead the development and testing of AI models for steel production processes, and a medium- to long-term master plan will be drawn up to spread those models to other companies.

RIST is the lead organization, working with the city of Pohang, the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation, Pohang Technopark and the Korea Institute of Industrial Technology. A total of 15 institutions are taking part, including steelmakers such as Dongkuk Steel and Jeil Technos, universities including POSTECH and Seoul National University, and AI and information technology specialists such as Konan Technology and CodeVision. Lee Kwan-hee, head of RIST's K-Steel Innovation Research Institute, said the institute will draw together close cooperation among industry, academia, research institutes and government to complete an AI innovation model optimized for the steel industry. He said the work aims to establish the Pohang complex as a model case for manufacturing AX in South Korea.

The project will be linked to an existing initiative to build a digitally based resource-circulation pilot complex. The plan is to promote recycling of byproducts generated during steel production and establish a resource-circulation system. Organizers pursue better production efficiency and an environmentally friendly industrial complex at the same time. The goal is to extend AI technology, now concentrated at a handful of companies, across the complex as a whole.

Articles.Title: Pohang Steel Complex Launches AI Project With 15 Partners - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Fadu Founder Starts AI Venture Amid Inflated-IPO Trial - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
stories.Summary:
Lee Ji-hyo, the former CEO of Fadu, started an artificial intelligence startup called Abundance in August, six months after leaving the chip design company. The new firm is based in Seoul's Gangnam district, has paid-in capital of 10 million won, and lists information and communications services and management consulting among its registered activities. Lee confirmed the move in a social media post on Oct. 14, saying he left Fadu in August. He wrote that Fadu had reached the stage where it needed to grow the opportunities it had secured, and that steadily expanding on existing achievements was not what he does best. Lee holds about 4.46 million Fadu shares, a 9% stake that made him the second-largest shareholder after CEO Nam Yi-hyun, who owns 12%.

The stake was worth about 295.8 billion won based on a closing price of 66,300 won, and the mandatory lock-up period on the shares expired in August. Fadu listed on the Kosdaq market in August 2023 at a valuation of 1.5 trillion won, projecting annual revenue of around 120 billion won. Revenue disclosed shortly after listing was 59 million won in the second quarter and 321 million won in the third quarter, and full-year revenue reached only 22.5 billion won. Prosecutors indicted Lee, Nam and Fadu as a corporate entity on Dec. 18 last year on charges of violating the Capital Markets Act. They allege management proceeded with the IPO despite knowing that major customers had suspended or reduced orders, and argued that Fadu failed to revise its revenue forecasts even though SK hynix had notified it of a halt to additional orders and SpaceX had suspended orders.

The trial is underway at the Seoul Southern District Court. Lee resigned as CEO in February, the day the Korea Exchange decided to resume trading in Fadu shares, and Fadu said at the time that he would leave the board but remain with the company. An investment industry official said that if the founder sells his stake while questions over accountability for the IPO controversy remain unresolved, it could undermine market confidence, and that he needs to clarify his position on retaining his shares with the trial ongoing. THE ELEC contacted Lee to ask whether he plans to keep his Fadu shares during the trial but received no response. Lee said he wants to work with talented Korean engineers to help change the world, from AI data centers to AI models.

Articles.Title: Fadu Founder Starts AI Venture Amid Inflated-IPO Trial - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Moore Agency’s M.Cast 2027 report calls next year an ‘AI hinge’ year
stories.Summary:
Tallahassee-based Moore Agency will release its third annual M.Cast trends report on Monday at the Public Relations Society of America's ICON conference in Orlando. The report calls 2027 an "AI hinge" year and argues the technology is moving into the middle of business, between brands and customers, leaders and the public, employers and workers, and workers and their own thinking. It says more of how audiences find and choose an organization will run through a machine first, and trust will become the competitive advantage. The report builds a "Trust Factor" section into each of its seven trends.

Terrie Ard, president and chief operating officer of Moore, will present the findings at ICON, which runs Oct. 18-20 at the Orlando World Center Marriott. The seven trends are The Orchestration Advantage, Verified Voices, Out of Sync, Cognitive Debt, Made by People, The Simple Button, and Intent Intelligence. Verified Voices covers what the report calls fake consensus, noting public comments and grassroots support can now be manufactured at speed. It cites a Los Angeles Times investigation in which a California air quality district received roughly 20,000 comments opposing a proposed pollution rule, and when it contacted a sample of 172 commenters, several said they knew nothing about comments filed under their names.

Cognitive Debt argues that mental muscles weaken as people hand more thinking to machines, citing an MIT Media Lab study that used EEGs on AI-assisted writers. It also cites BCG research finding workers most involved in AI oversight showed 33% more decision fatigue and 39% higher intent to quit. Ard said organizations can no longer afford to wait for certainty, and that leaders who thrive will identify emerging signals and decide where technology should lead and where human judgment remains essential. She also said the machine gets stronger but the human must too, and that success in 2027 will belong to leaders who move quickly with technology while preserving judgment, relationships, and trust.

Intent Intelligence cites Accenture research finding 54% of people usually get everything they need from an AI summary, and two-thirds now use AI search weekly. The report proposes an "Influence Ladder" with five rungs: delivered, seen, noticed, remembered, and acted on. Moore, founded by Karen Moore, is a women-owned agency headquartered in Tallahassee with team members nationwide, and it reports a 98% client retention rate. The full report is available at MCastTrends.com.

Articles.Title: Moore Agency’s M.Cast 2027 report calls next year an ‘AI hinge’ year

stories.Headline: AI platform allows real-time conversation between patients and their medical devices
stories.Summary:
A new AI-driven platform let patients undergoing seizure monitoring send messages to their brain-monitoring devices and get feedback in real time, according to findings published in Nature Medicine by researchers at the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine and its Center for Neuroengineering and Therapeutics. The proof-of-concept study enrolled 13 adults receiving continuous electroencephalogram (EEG) monitoring in Penn's Epilepsy Monitoring Unit, admitted to find the source of their seizures or as part of presurgical evaluation. The platform was built by a team of Penn Bioengineering Ph.D. students led by Zack Goldblum, Haoer Shi and Zhongchuan Xu. It had three parts: software that continuously captured EEG data from electrodes in the brain, a secure HIPAA-compliant cloud environment that analyzed the information in near real time, and a smartphone application with a Penn-developed AI conversational agent similar to the technology behind ChatGPT.

Through the app, patients could ask questions about their brain activity, request visualizations of trends in their data, report symptoms and receive alerts or surveys throughout the day, in text, charts and other formats. The device could also contact patients when it saw changes that might interest them and learn on the fly from their responses. Researchers analyzed 1,307 messages exchanged between patients and the system, most about seizure events, sleep, mood, energy levels and other factors that can influence seizure activity. Patients were surveyed three times daily about sleep, anxiety, mood, well-being and other symptoms, and several said the platform helped explain patterns they had noticed but struggled to understand.

Senior author Brian Litt, M.D., a professor of neurology, neurosurgery and bioengineering, said the idea is that instead of waiting for a specialist to analyze the data collected by your device, the device could detect changes and alert you immediately, like your own personal Jiminy Cricket on your shoulder. He said both the patient and the device can learn together over time, with the device learning what matters to the patient and the patient learning how their behavior affects their health. Patients could teach the system which seizures it correctly identified and which were false alarms, and clinicians could converse with it to review its assessments and add their own notations through a smart expert-in-the-loop algorithm. Litt said patients often understand aspects of their disease that sensors cannot measure directly.

The team believes the platform could have broad applications for conditions that use cardiac devices, insulin pumps and emerging treatments for neuropsychiatric disorders such as Parkinson's disease, depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, addiction and cognitive disorders. Researchers envision systems that can automatically adjust treatment while communicating directly with patients about symptoms and treatment goals, and the team is already preparing studies with Lauren Hammer, M.D., Ph.D., an assistant professor of neurology and bioengineering, to apply the platform to automatically tune deep brain stimulation devices for Parkinson's disease. Further work is incorporating wearables into applications for insomnia, epilepsy, brain and vital signs monitoring. Ongoing research will evaluate whether the platform can reduce seizure frequency and severity, improve quality of life, decrease emergency department visits and lower health care utilization, and researchers plan to expand testing into outpatient settings using newer minimally invasive EEG and wearable technologies.

Articles.Title: AI platform allows real-time conversation between patients and their medical devices

stories.Headline: English Department, Herbert Writing Center facing AI increase in student writing
stories.Summary:
AI is increasingly appearing in student writing at the University of Tennessee, and the English Department is working to preserve human voice and authenticity. Kirsten Benson, executive director of UT’s Herbert Writing Center, said she sees students being more emphatic about wanting to preserve that human voice and the authenticity of their own ideas. The writing center does often see AI use in students’ work, and it has learned ways students can use AI responsibly and productively. Benson said students should start from their own mind, knowledge and resources, and use AI in ways that assist their writing process rather than replace it. The English Department has changed its coursework to lessen students’ reliance on AI.

Dawn Coleman, head of the English Department and an English professor, said the department now has far fewer discussion posts, take-home exams and summary paragraphs, because those assignments can be very tempting for students to use AI on. Coleman said the department tries to focus on aspects of learning that call for people to draw on their own direct experiences or very careful engagement with texts as discussed in class. Assignments based more on opinion and experience make AI easier to detect in student work and harder for students to use AI to complete writing assignments. Benson said AI can be a productive tool if students use their own ideas throughout the process and keep their voice in the work. She said seeing another way to do something and learning from it can be integrated into a writer’s own repertoire, and that this is true of human feedback as well as AI feedback.

She said the long-term productivity of AI use depends on how much the student gains from the experience. If a student simply copy-and-pastes AI feedback, they will not learn anything, but if they observe and learn how AI articulates an idea, they can use that in their own writing in the future without AI. As AI continues to grow, staying educated on its proper use is a responsibility for both students and faculty at UT, the article says. The English Department is taking steps to stop students from using AI tools, but it is aware it cannot completely eliminate them. Students must remember the importance and power of their own voice in their writing, which the article says can never be replicated.

Articles.Title: English Department, Herbert Writing Center facing AI increase in student writing

stories.Headline: Value Options: Micron, the AI Boom, and the Hidden Opportunities in Deep Value Stocks
stories.Summary:
Tobias Carlisle and Tim Travis discussed AI stocks, Micron and deep value stocks on the Value Options Letter podcast, in an episode published on October 18, 2026. They said the market had been miserable for about 50 days and that business values felt detached from stock prices. Travis compared the mood to 2011, when big banks traded at fractions of tangible book value, and to 2021, when meme stocks crashed the next year. Carlisle said long run rates keep rising and energy trades near a hundred dollars, which hurts small value cyclical stocks first.

The hosts said the biggest 10 AI and AI CapEx companies are carrying the market while everything else underperforms. Carlisle said highly profitable companies reached seven times book value in 2000 and now sit at 11 times book value. Travis said the hyperscalers are spending about $600 billion and depreciation might be one fifth or one sixth of that, so earnings take a smaller hit than free cash flow. He said Micron trades at 5.41 forward earnings and is sold out for about two years, but China is starting to get into the memory game.

Carlisle said Micron has traditionally been very cyclical and pops into deep value screens all the time, and he does not know whether the nature of the business has changed. Travis said the memory business is an oligopoly with two or three major suppliers, which changed the dynamics and produced insane margins. He raised the point, which he credited to Steve Eisman, that if people lose confidence in OpenAI and Anthropic, big order books at companies like Oracle might come into question. Carlisle said the hyperscalers are still decent values and called Meta dirt cheap for a while.

Both hosts said AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT are powerful and they use them all day, while about 95% of people do not use the paid versions. Carlisle compared the moment to the late 1990s and early 2000s dot-com boom, which was game changing but got ahead of itself before collapsing. He said it took 10 or 15 years for the internet to be properly integrated into business everywhere. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Value Options: Micron, the AI Boom, and the Hidden Opportunities in Deep Value Stocks

stories.Headline: Beyond Workflow Automation: Agentic AI Readiness
stories.Summary:
Workflow software is moving from fixed task routing to platforms that coordinate work across agents, software, automation and people, according to FTI Consulting. This agentic software can interpret goals, decide actions, gather context, use tools and adapt as conditions change. FTI published its assessment on October 18, 2026. The shift changes both the role and the economics of enterprise software.

Gartner estimates up to $234 billion, about 20% of enterprise application SaaS spending, could be exposed to agentic arbitrage by 2030. FTI gave an illustrative underwriting case, not a forecast, in which seat revenue on agent-addressable accounts falls 20% to 40% over a renewal cycle. If outcome-based pricing replaces only half of the lost revenue and inference costs move into cost of goods sold, gross margins could fall more than 70% to below 60%. FTI said the actual impact will depend on workflow exposure, pricing power, adoption and delivery economics. Gartner also predicts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by 2027, and 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous agents by 2027.

FTI assessed 57 providers across six dimensions and grouped them into Workflow Execution Readiness and Enterprise Reach. It identified six warning signs, including fragmented workflow context, AI that augments tasks but cannot complete workflows, integration that stops at connectivity, weak enterprise controls, economics still tied to human seats, and bespoke pilot-led deployments. FTI said integration platforms and AI-native providers generally show stronger execution readiness but more limited enterprise reach. Traditional workflow and business process management providers appear more exposed when differentiation rests on visualization, basic connectors, routing logic, limited proprietary context or seat-based pricing. FTI said category alone does not determine readiness and the matrix is meant to diagnose gaps, not pick winners.

FTI listed six priorities for investors and management teams: map the current state, quantify economic exposure, pressure-test the roadmap, prioritize defensible workflows, close capability gaps and track execution. It said workflows will stay hybrid, with automation for stable work, agents for variable work and people for decisions that are material, regulated or ambiguous. UiPath Maestro coordinates agents, robots, systems and people across governed workflows, and ServiceNow reports AI and automation supporting 89% of self-service requests and 37% of customer-support case workflow. FTI said the key risk is not a lack of AI features.

Articles.Title: Beyond Workflow Automation: Agentic AI Readiness

stories.Headline: OpenCode Security Breach: Distillation Attack Hit Console Users With Linked AI Providers. How to Find OpenCode on Developer Machines and Respond
stories.Summary:
On October 18, 2026, OpenCode, the open source AI coding agent, disclosed a security breach tied to what it called a large scale distillation attack. The breach affected 1.4% of OpenCode Console users, specifically those who had external AI providers linked. The providers named are Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. OpenCode said it notified every impacted user by email on the morning of October 18, and that anyone who did not receive an email was not impacted. The incident is ongoing, and OpenCode has not published a root cause or said what data was accessed.

OpenCode has not published a list of affected versions. According to the vendor statement, the breach is tied to OpenCode Console accounts with linked external providers, not to a specific release of the OpenCode CLI, so the installed version alone does not show whether a developer was impacted. What matters is whether a developer has an OpenCode Console account and linked an Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google provider to it. OpenCode stores linked provider credentials on the developer's machine at ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json on macOS and Linux, and at %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\auth.json on Windows. If that file exists and lists a provider, the developer should be treated as potentially affected until OpenCode's email confirms otherwise.

OpenCode said it is working with Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google to remediate, and that the incident is ongoing so it cannot share more details at this point. The article advises checking for an email from OpenCode, since the vendor says no email means not impacted. It also advises checking which providers are linked in the auth.json file, rotating any Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google API keys connected to OpenCode or the OpenCode Console, and reviewing each provider's usage dashboard for requests the developer did not make. The article notes that developers link AI provider accounts so the agent can call models on their behalf, and that exposed credentials could let an attacker run inference against the victim's provider account, showing up as unexpected spend.

The article says most security teams do not have a list of which developers run which AI coding agents, so the first job is to find out who has OpenCode installed. It describes checking manually for the OpenCode binary and its data directories, or using the free, open source StepSecurity Dev Machine Guard, which detects OpenCode out of the box. StepSecurity customers can see which users and devices run OpenCode from the Coding Tools page and the Threat Center, though that does not show who has a Console account or which providers they linked. The article says it will keep the post updated as OpenCode and the named providers share more.

Articles.Title: OpenCode Security Breach: Distillation Attack Hit Console Users With Linked AI Providers. How to Find OpenCode on Developer Machines and Respond

stories.Headline: AI company Databricks doubling footprint at 5 Bryant Park
stories.Summary:
Databricks is doubling its footprint at 5 Bryant Park to 120,000 square feet across five floors, the New York Post reported on October 18, 2026. The data and AI company, which occupies space at the Savanna-owned building, plans to enlarge its engineering and research headcounts. Details of the lease were not released. The expansion more than doubles the company's presence in the Manhattan building.

The move requires the company to grow its engineering and research teams in the city. Databricks' vice-president of engineering in the city, Tasso Argyros, wrote on his corporate blog that earlier this year the company made a bet that world-class AI would be built in Manhattan. He said that bet is paying off today. Argyros described New York as the global nerve center for financial services, media, healthcare and retail, and said these companies are where AI gets shaped in the real world.

Argyros also cited the city's talent-rich ecosystem. He said top new graduates increasingly want to build their careers in New York, and that Databricks gives them the chance to work on problems at the frontier of data and AI without leaving the city. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned hiring and the expanded space. More to follow.

Articles.Title: AI company Databricks doubling footprint at 5 Bryant Park

stories.Headline: Gloo awards $200,000 in AI hackathon
stories.Summary:
Gloo Holdings Inc., a Boulder company that provides artificial intelligence and technology platforms for faith-based organizations, awarded $200,000 in prizes during its 2026 AI Hackathon. A team from Austin Christian University claimed the $100,000 grand prize for Fosterly, an AI tool that helps young people leaving the Texas foster-care system. The project uses AI to connect young adults aging out of foster care with services and people who can help them move to independent living. More than 1,000 participants on more than 115 teams competed in the event.

The hackathon began Sept. 8 with a 30-day virtual development period and ended with an in-person competition Oct. 6-8 at the Limelight Hotel in Boulder. The theme was “Building Together: Humans, Agents and the Future of Flourishing,” and the event was open to people with varying degrees of technical experience. Three other teams received $20,000 each for winning individual categories. Austin Christian University’s Unify team won the Best of Agents category for an AI system that helps nonprofits consolidate software functions that might otherwise require as many as 20 separate applications.

Frontier Commons won the Best of Ministry Resourcing category for OnBoard, a tool that helps missionaries communicate with donors by collecting and organizing information for newsletters and updates. Envoy Mission won the Best of Bible category for an offline, private Bible application disguised as an ordinary app, intended for people in countries where possession of a Bible could lead to imprisonment. Gloo awarded another $40,000 among winners in additional categories. Entries were judged on concepts, innovation, potential impact, use of AI and presentations.

Gloo co-founder and CEO Scott Beck said in a prepared statement that Gloo believes AI should be shaped for good, reflecting the needs, values and aspirations of the faith and flourishing ecosystem. He said the hackathon turns that belief into action. Judges included Beck, Eric Célérier, CEO of HelloBible, Pat Gelsinger, executive chair and head of technology at Gloo, and Scott Mosely, vice president of software at RightNowMedia. A complete list of winners is available at gloo.com/hackathon.

Articles.Title: Gloo awards $200,000 in AI hackathon

stories.Headline: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
stories.Summary:
TinyFish, a web infrastructure company for AI agents, announced free search and fetch access within set rate limits. The company made the move to remove its retrieval charge for agents reading the web. On the September 28, 2026 Artificial Analysis snapshot, TinyFish Search (web) scored 71 at $9.30 per 1,000 benchmark tasks. Each task took 59.0 seconds, counting model and search time. The free tier allows 30 search requests per minute and 500 per hour, plus 150 fetched URLs per minute and 1,000 per day.

TinyFish had the lowest total cost among the 12 configurations shown on the leaderboard. The highest displayed score was Perplexity Search (medium) at 80, and the lowest was TinyFish Search (web) at 71. The no-search baseline was 33, and TinyFish also had the second longest time per task among displayed configurations. TinyFish argues that teams budget for the model and underestimate how much retrieved content drives cost. A June 2, 2026 fetch quality evaluation across 45 URLs and 5 providers found large differences in returned page size.

For one Daily Mail article of roughly 4,300 characters, TinyFish Fetch returned 4,737 characters, while Firecrawl Scrape returned 171,095. The company said retrieval charges are only one part of the cost, since returned content still enters the model as input tokens. The articles do not say who at TinyFish is responsible or what executives said beyond the company's argument about costs. They also do not say what happens next. More to follow.

Articles.Title: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web

stories.Headline: GTIA: AI Talk Is How MSPs Can Get Clients To Do Basic Security Like MFA
stories.Summary:
Lisa Person, director of cybersecurity engagement programs at GTIA, said managed service providers can get clients to adopt basic security measures by talking about the risks of AI. She made the point in a Sunday keynote at the XChange NexGen 2026 conference in Orlando, Florida, hosted by CRN parent company The Channel Company. A GTIA survey of more than 300 MSPs in North America in the third quarter found that many clients have not adopted very basic protections. Person said MSPs can stress the threats posed by AI, whether clients use it or malicious actors do.

The survey found that only 46 percent of MSP customers have DNS filtering deployed, and just 42 percent have multifactor authentication enabled for critical systems. Adoption was even lower for managed detection and response at 37 percent and immutable backups at 35 percent. At the same time, MSPs reported that 75 percent of their customers are willing to pay more for cybersecurity services as costs rise. Person said these conversations are the perfect time for MSPs to go back to clients and fix security gaps they have not seen before.

Person cited remarks by Corey Kirkendoll, vice chair of GTIA's AI Advisory Council and CEO of 5K Technical Services in Allen, Texas. She said that while people were tired of talking about cybersecurity and did not want to pay more for it, talk of AI and agents running loose in systems makes clients ask how to control them. That brings them back to basics and basic controls, she said. Person added that MSPs say their clients know AI is creating awareness and hear about it in the news all the time, so now is the opportunity.

Jeremy Hall, a business account manager at Dallas-based Qnet Managed Services, told CRN the presentation showed how important it is for MSPs to bundle security services and products for clients. He said MSPs should show clients up front that a bundle will take care of their network and their laptops, rather than coming to them at different times with different things. Person said that as MSPs have these conversations, it is the perfect time to fix security gaps. She said clients already know AI is out there, so now is the opportunity to act.

Articles.Title: GTIA: AI Talk Is How MSPs Can Get Clients To Do Basic Security Like MFA

stories.Headline: Intuit Bets on AI-Powered Revenue Automation with Sequence Acquisition
stories.Summary:
Intuit announced on Thursday that it will acquire Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform founded in 2021. The deal expands Intuit's revenue management offerings for mid-market businesses. Sequence uses AI to help B2B finance and commercial teams automate the full quote-to-revenue lifecycle, including deal configuration and pricing, billing, invoicing, collections, and revenue recognition. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The acquisition will strengthen Intuit Enterprise Suite, a resource planning and consolidation platform, and QuickBooks Online Advanced, its cloud-based accounting platform. It will also expand Intuit's reach to sectors including B2B software, professional services, construction, healthcare, and manufacturing. Intuit held $4.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents and had total debt of $7.7 billion as of July 31. Intuit also reiterated its fiscal 2027 guidance, expecting revenue between $23.279 billion and $23.512 billion, GAAP EPS of $20.12 to $20.36, and adjusted EPS of $22.88 to $23.12.

Sequence co-founder and CEO Riya Grover highlighted the growing need for revenue management automation as business complexity grows with usage-based and hybrid pricing models. Ashley Still, executive vice president and general manager of Intuit's Small Business & Mid-Market Group, said the acquisition extends Intuit Enterprise Suite into industries that increasingly use AI consumption models. She called it a meaningful step toward delivering AI-native ERP for complex businesses. Following the acquisition, Grover and the Sequence team will join Intuit's Mid-Market product organization.

Intuit stock rose more than 6% on Thursday after the announcement. The stock carries a Buy rating with an average price forecast of $378. Intuit reiterated its first quarter and full year fiscal 2027 guidance in conjunction with its Investor Day on Sept. 17. It expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $4.29 billion and $4.31 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.44 to $2.48.

Articles.Title: Intuit Bets on AI-Powered Revenue Automation with Sequence Acquisition

stories.Headline: Netanyahu Accuses Russia Of Aiding Iran, Running Antisemitic AI Bot Networks
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday accused Russia of aiding Iran and using artificial intelligence to run antisemitic bot networks targeting Israel and Jews worldwide. He made the accusation in response to a question from i24NEWS. He said Israel and Russia have conflicting interests but still share some common ground. The remarks marked a shift in tone from his long-standing portrayal of his relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin as an important asset.

Netanyahu said he remains in occasional contact with Putin and speaks with him when necessary. He also suggested that Putin does not want Iran to acquire nuclear weapons. He argued that a nuclear-armed Tehran could threaten Russia's own interests. Among the risks he cited was the possibility that Iran could recruit Muslim groups inside Russia to act on its behalf.

Netanyahu is the one making the accusations, and he delivered them publicly while acknowledging the two countries' differences. He described his contacts with Putin as occasional and said they happen when needed. He said he believes Putin also opposes a nuclear-armed Iran. The articles do not say what evidence, if any, was presented for the claims about Russia or the bot networks.

The articles give no response from Russia or from Putin to the accusations. They also give no details on what happens next beyond Netanyahu's remarks. The piece notes that his public accusations highlight tensions between the two countries. More to follow.
